record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: Give an analytic interpretation, valid for every n >= 2, of the matrix P_2 of first syzygies in the free resolution of the n-dimensional Cauchy-Fueter module M_n. The matrix P_2 encodes compatibility conditions for the non-homogeneous Cauchy-Fueter system d f / d bar(q_i) = g_i; for n = 2 these conditions have a simple quaternionic form, but for n = 3 the known 12 by 40 matrix gives ten quaternionic second-order compatibility conditions that the source says are not yet analytically understood.

evidence.quote: Problem: Give an analytic interpretation for the matrix P_2 of the first syzygies, for any n >= 2.
The matrix P_2 which appears in Theorem 3.2 is particularly important because it allows us to write explicitly the compatibility conditions for the non-homogeneous system.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of real quaternions, written $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$, and for $n \geq 2$ consider $n$ quaternionic variables $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ with $q_\ell = x_{\ell,0} + x_{\ell,1} i + x_{\ell,2} j + x_{\ell,3} k$. The Cauchy–Fueter operator in the variable $q_\ell$ is
$$\frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{q}_\ell} \;=\; \frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,0}} + i\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,1}} + j\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,2}} + k\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,3}}.$$
Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the polynomial ring (or its appropriate Fourier-transformed analogue) modeling these $n$ Cauchy–Fueter operators, and let $P_1$ be the matrix representing the operator $f \mapsto (\partial f/\partial \bar{q}_1, \ldots, \partial f/\partial \bar{q}_n)$. The Cauchy–Fueter module is $M_n = \operatorname{coker} P_1^t$. In a minimal free resolution
$$\cdots \longrightarrow \mathcal{R}^{a_2} \xrightarrow{P_2} \mathcal{R}^{a_1} \xrightarrow{P_1} \mathcal{R}^{a_0} \longrightarrow M_n \longrightarrow 0,$$
the matrix $P_2$ of first syzygies encodes the compatibility conditions that an $n$-tuple $(g_1, \ldots, g_n)$ of quaternion-valued functions must satisfy in order for the non-homogeneous system
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{q}_\ell} \;=\; g_\ell, \qquad \ell = 1, \ldots, n,$$
to admit a solution $f$. For $n = 2$ these compatibility conditions admit a simple quaternionic expression; for $n = 3$ one obtains a $12 \times 40$ matrix encoding ten quaternionic second-order compatibility conditions whose analytic/geometric meaning is not transparent.

Problem. Give an analytic interpretation, valid uniformly for every $n \geq 2$, of the matrix $P_2$ of first syzygies in the free resolution of the Cauchy–Fueter module $M_n$ — that is, describe the compatibility conditions imposed by $P_2$ on the right-hand side $(g_1, \ldots, g_n)$ in a conceptual analytic form (analogous to the way curl-type conditions arise in the several complex variables $\bar\partial$-problem).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published analytic interpretation of the first-syzygy matrix $P_2$ in the free resolution of the $n$-variable Cauchy–Fueter module valid for all $n \geq 2$. Related work (e.g., on $k$-Cauchy–Fueter operators and Bochner–Martinelli-type formulas) treats specific aspects but does not appear to resolve this conceptual question, so the status is taken as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems on the Analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter System in Several Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Listed among open problems concerning the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several quaternionic variables.
status_evidence.claim: The analytic interpretation of P_2 is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Bochner–Martinelli formula for k-Cauchy–Fueter operator
status_evidence.snippet: Analytic tools for k-Cauchy–Fueter operators developed via explicit kernels, but does not address syzygy interpretation in general n.
status_evidence.claim: Related analytic developments do not appear to resolve the general syzygy interpretation.
